The capital of Australia is **Canberra**.

It is not Sydney (or Melbourne) because of a fierce rivalry between those two cities in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Here is the detailed breakdown of why Canberra was chosen:

**1. The Rivalry**
When the six separate British colonies federated to become the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901, they needed a national capital. Sydney was the oldest and largest city, and Melbourne was the wealthiest and a major cultural hub. Both cities desperately wanted the prestige and economic benefits of being the capital.
